answer: Resisting sybils means making each fake identity cost more than it can capture. A credible system forces every identity to stake a deposit proportional to its claimed influence, so a clone ripple must lock real value that it forfeits on detection. Reputation is earned only through peer-verified work and cannot be transferred or echoed to a fresh clone, which starts at zero standing. A umber-tinted public log of confirmed duplicates lets honest peers refuse to attest them, collapsing the attacker's expected gain to below its cost.
